E1.quote: I skip extra device screens when the patient needs me at the bedside.

E2.quote: Training usually happens in a short huddle before the shift.

E3.quote: I double check the dose before I start the pump.

E4.quote: When an alarm is vague I ask another nurse before restarting.

E5.quote: A long setup makes me write a reminder on the room board.

E6.quote: I want the alarm to tell me exactly what needs attention.

E7.quote: I test changes on a bench unit before they reach a floor.

E8.quote: Logs matter because I need to reproduce a fault.

E9.quote: I avoid firmware changes during active clinical use.

E10.quote: A clear error code shortens troubleshooting.

E11.quote: I ask nursing staff what happened immediately before a fault.

E12.quote: Network drops can look like device failures.

E13.quote: I document every configuration used in a test.

E14.quote: I need service manuals to match the deployed software.

E15.quote: I compare repeated alarms across devices before blaming hardware.

E16.quote: I prefer changes that can be rolled back.

E17.quote: Shift pressure makes optional documentation less likely.

E18.quote: A bedside workaround can hide a recurring technical issue.
